vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Security fixes skip the night window and the shared group: their own pull request, merged once CI passes

android-platforms.description: Reads the Android API levels from Google's Android SDK repository manifest

android-platforms-minor.description: Reads the full Android API levels (major.minor, such as 37.1) from Google's Android SDK repository manifest, skipping beta and extension builds

agp-from-catalog.description: Reads the agp version from the main branch version catalog of the yasan-org repository named by the package name

customManagers.description: Track the Android compile SDK in the version catalog
Track the Android target SDK in the version catalog

Track the Android Gradle Plugin through toolkit's version catalog rather than Maven, so this catalog only moves to an AGP that toolkit already builds with: projects that include both need one AGP version

packageRules.description: kotlinx-datetime's -compat builds are a compatibility artifact for 0.6.x consumers, not newer releases
The agp version moves through the android-gradle-plugin custom manager, which follows toolkit's catalog, so the Gradle manager leaves every dependency on it alone
Every update lands in one pull request, merged once CI passes; last so it overrides the presets' groups

Android API level bumps get their own pull request and wait for a person: a new compile SDK can need a newer Android Gradle Plugin, and a new target SDK changes how the sample behaves on devices, which CI does not see; after the shared group so it wins
